$comment: Sun and moon shadows on the distant terrain (docs/DAY_NIGHT.md §12, ADR 0046): the lighting's third layer, past the shadow cascades (shadows.json). The renderer draws the terrain as drawn (chunks, LOD sections) from above into heightmaps around the eye, a slice of the casters a frame, and the scene's shaders march each far fragment's ray toward the light over them: mountains shade valleys at dusk. It follows the Shadows setting (Off draws none; a CPU adapter draws none). Run `node shared/look/lodshadows.mjs` after editing; CI fails if crates/dwell-look/src/lodshadows.gen.rs is stale.

heights.$comment: The face-local heights the maps hold (m over the midplane): below bottomM nothing casts; topM is over every terrain and build.

march.$comment: startTexels: the ray's first step from the fragment (texels of the map it reads). normalOffsetTexels: the ray starts this many texels out along the surface's normal. biasM: and this far up (against a surface shading itself through the map's coarse texels). penumbraDeg: a ray this far under the horizon it meets is wholly in shade, this far over it wholly lit (a painterly soft edge; the sun's disc is about ½°). edgeFade: the shadows fade out over this last share of the outermost map's half-width, so its edge never shows.

tiers.$comment: Per Shadows setting. resolution: each map's texels a side (a power of two). texelM: the nearest map's texel (m). levels: how many maps (1–2), each next one levelScale times coarser around the same eye. steps: the march's steps, spaced from the first step to reachM geometrically (fine near the fragment, coarse far off). fillKtris, fillDraws: each frame draws at most this many thousand triangles and draws into the map being filled (one map at a time, in turn; it replaces the one shown when it is whole), so the cost is spread over frames and never spikes.
